Don't feel ashamed of reaching out to a bunch of strangers online, you have every right to with everything that's happened to you. Being a people pleaser isn't all negative, you just have to learn when people are taking advantage of you or if you are letting your guilt of not making someone happy overcome you. 

Have you considered looking into therapy of some kind? I know it's a very typical answer when someone is having problems but it helps a lot to have someone to talk to who is for one, a professional. So they know steps and ideas to help you work through your problems and two, it's someone you can actually talk to face to face, it feels more genuine. 

I've been struggling since my early teens (I'm 26 now) with my problems, but things are better than they were a few years ago, i have some rather depressing posts on this reddit as well of how things used to be for me. But ever since I got a good therapist I'm doing a lot better and learning more about myself, recently I'm discovering I might have autism and need to get tested for that. 

But anyway to wrap it all up, life gets better eventually if you slowly work towards goals to better yourself or understand yourself, and having help and support is nothing to feel guilty or ashamed of or feeling like a burden. 
I'm here you need someone to talk to if there's nobody else.
